_about: French's chapter 4 run of Tabletop as data: the configuration of Fig. 4.1, and for each of the nine screen dumps (Figs. 4.1-4.9) the codelets run, the thermometer, the 41 Slipnet boxes, the Coderack bar graph and the structures drawn, every number read on the page image at 300 dpi (600 dpi for the doubtful cells) [F95 pp. 95-107]; then the five partial dumps of other runs (Figs. 4.10-4.14) [F95 pp. 108-110]. French's narration is quoted, with the machine-checked tags, in docs/ch4-run.md; here it is paraphrased. Doubtful readings are listed under 'doubtful'. Checked by tests/test_ch4.py.
pdf_offset: PDF page = printed page + 11 for pp. 47-111

the Worldview is incoherent (it lacks systematicity), the cup-cup correspondence being off by itself; had cup-glass been put in competition it would almost certainly have won by making the Worldview coherent; either the program never noticed the potential cup-glass correspondence, or it was suggested and defeated by cup-cup

narration.what: the figure includes the temperature and shows the effect of high temperature: a cup-spoon grouping rarely survives, the program being highly unlikely to group objects of such disparate categories
